subject: Post-call: Astrum Health model-fit & eval playbook + next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@astrumhealth.com>, Tanya Kim <tanya.kim@astrumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Astrum model-fit & proposed eval playbook

Thanks again for your time today — quick recap and proposed next steps to get a customer-specific eval running on Redwood. I kept this high-level so we can iterate quickly.

Call highlights (what I heard)
- Goal: automate triage summarization + suggested care pathways from intake notes (sensitivity to clinical correctness).
- Success metrics: precision@top1 for actionable recommendations >= 78%, clinically critical errors = 0 tolerable, overall latency target for live inference < 250ms P50 under pilot traffic.
- Data availability: will share ~2.5k de-identified intake records initially; expect full set (~25k) within 6 weeks.

Proposed eval playbook (initial run)
1) Dataset & format: you’ll share a JSONL sample (one example per line) with fields: id, input_text, expected_actions (CSV string), and reviewer_label (one of: OK / unsafe / needs_review). See attached sample (astrum_sample_subset.jsonl).
2) Prompt bank: use the attached prompt_set_v1.csv as the starting prompt bank. We recommend templating for slot-filling + an instruction-only variant.
3) Models to include: rw-compact-7b-v1 (fast baseline), rw-gpt-13b-v2 (higher quality), and a quantized 13B variant we can stage if you want to measure cost/latency tradeoffs. Ben will share precise model IDs and cost estimates.
4) Scoring rubric: primary metric = precision@1 on suggested action (binary match with expected_actions), secondary = reviewer_label distribution and an FNR on clinically critical labels. See redwood_eval_rubric_v1.md attached for details.
5) Regression guardrails: we will run the new models side-by-side with a control snapshot and surface candidate regressions by prompt set + slice. We recommend an initial acceptance threshold of no more than 2% drop in precision@1 vs control on the pilot dataset.

Next steps (action owners)
- Astrum (Jared/Tanya): upload the 2.5k de-identified sample to the Drive link and confirm column semantics (today/Mon). Attachments OK.
- Redwood (Irene): provision the evaluation job, create shared scoring dashboard, and provide a Jupyter snippet to compute metrics (by Mon).
- Redwood (Ben): publish recommended model variants + expected token costs and P50 latency estimates for the sample distribution (Mon/Tue).

Notes / asks
- If you can flag any examples that are especially sensitive (PHI edge-cases), add a field sensitive:true so we can exclude them from public metrics.
- If there are regulatory constraints around retention/audit, mention that and we’ll enable the Private deployment runbook.

Attachments: astrum_prompt_set_v1.csv (prompt templates), astrum_sample_subset.jsonl (10 records), redwood_eval_rubric_v1.md

I’ll stand up the eval skeleton as soon as the sample lands. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@astrumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Astrum model-fit & proposed eval playbook

Perfect — thanks Jared. Confirmed receipt of the Drive files. Quick refinements and commitments from our side: 

What we’ll run (committed)
- Three generation variants as requested (instruction+context, instruction-only, constrained short-answer).
- Models: rw-compact-7b-v1 (baseline), rw-gpt-13b-v2 (primary), rw-gpt-13b-quant (cost/latency variant).
- Evaluation slices: by reviewer_label, by patient_age_bucket, and by action taxonomy group.

Scoring details (concrete)
- Primary metric: precision@1 where match = exact normalized action id (we will apply your action_taxonomy.csv mapping during normalization).
- Metric computation: for multi-action expected_actions we use: match if any expected action equals suggested action. Precision@1 = (#matches)/(#examples where model emitted suggestion).
- Clinical-safety audit: we’ll flag any example where reviewer_label == 'unsafe' and exclude from public dashboards; we will still surface counts and qualitative examples privately.

Data and access requests (what I need from Astrum)
- Confirm the Drive link is fine for the eval job (we will pull via service account). If you prefer S3, share creds.
- Please confirm the mapping file column name for normalized_id (so our normalizer knows which column to join on).
- If possible, provide 100 annotated examples where reviewers wrote free-text justifications — we’ll use them to seed a small human-in-the-loop scorer to validate borderline cases.

Timing & deliverables
- Redwood will queue the initial eval run today (Mon) against the 2.5k sample. Expect a results snapshot + dashboard link within 24–36 hours.
- Ben will post the model perf/cost summary by EOD Tue.

I’ll post the eval run link when it’s live and tag you.

Thanks — small ask: once you see the dashboard, flag 3 examples that feel the most representative (good/bad) so we can prioritize follow-up tuning.

Best,
Irene

On Mon, Apr 26, 2026 at 11:03 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Adding some specifics on model choices and regression guardrails.
> 
> Quick model notes:
> - rw-compact-7b-v1: 1–2x cheaper, P50 latency ~110–160ms on your average sample length (est). Good baseline for throughput tests.
> - rw-gpt-13b-v2: higher quality/precision, estimated P50 latency ~210–280ms; likely best for pilot acceptance.
> - rw-gpt-13b-quant: 8-bit quant variant targeted at cost-sensitive production with modest quality delta; we’ll validate any quality regression on the pilot sample.
> 
> Regression guardrails we will enforce in the job:
> - Compare candidate vs control snapshot on the same prompt bank and slices. Alert if precision@1 delta <= -0.02 (i.e., >2% drop).
> - For clinically critical action groups (we’ll label them once we ingest the taxonomy), require no FNR increase > 1%.
> - Automated diffing will surface representative examples; we’ll include an automated slack alert to your team when thresholds are breached.
> 
> Cost/ops note: if you move to Dedicated for the production rollout, your cost per 1k tokens served will be substantially lower and we can schedule a longer stability run. Procurement email OK to loop in when you’re ready.
> 
> — Ben
> Product Solutions, Redwood Inference
